A progressive decrease in lactase is noted from approximately 1–5 years of age through adolescence. Reported rates in United
States African-American children ranged from 27% lactose maldigestion following lactose testing using a lactose load equivalent
to two 8-ounce glasses of milk at 1–2 years to 74% in 11–12-year-old children. The progressive decrease in the ability to hydrolyze
a lactose challenge was observed in children of both high and low socioeconomic status. Studies in white children 1–12 years of age
identiﬁed only 17% of children maldigesting a lactose challenge. Signs and symptom production associated with a reduction in
lactose digestion in a child population is difﬁcult to measure due to the nature of the symptoms being reported and the signs
